standards_review.notes: 14 of 16 commit subjects use the documented EPMCDME-####: Description format; two do not: 'teams-integ-2-migration: add planning artifacts' and 'teams-integ-1-foundation: add planning artifacts'

New/modified files carry the Apache header, new functions use modern union/generic type hints (str | None, list[str]), no changed line exceeds the configured 120-char Ruff line-length, and the new validate_ms_teams_request/check_ms_teams_singleton paths are covered by new unit tests

Migration SQL uses bound parameters (sa.text with bindparams/JSONB, no string-interpolated values); create_project_setting now runs _check_permission before any credential validation instead of after; ms_teams assistant_ids are strictly type-checked (non-string entries rejected with 400 instead of failing later in set()/join()); the read-then-write singleton check is backed by a DB partial unique index and callers convert the resulting IntegrityError into a 409 instead of a raw 500; no credentials or tokens are logged in the changed code

blocking_findings.location: commit 'teams-integ-2-migration: add planning artifacts' and commit 'teams-integ-1-foundation: add planning artifacts'
blocking_findings.violation: git-workflow.md requires 'EPMCDME-####: Description' commit subjects; these two planning-artifact commits omit the ticket prefix entirely
blocking_findings.why_blocking: a non-conforming commit subject breaks the documented ticket-traceable history the git-workflow guide requires for repository commits
blocking_findings.remedy: reword the two commits (or fold them into an adjacent EPMCDME-14111 commit) so every subject carries the EPMCDME-14111: prefix
